Subject: RE: Production latency + error spike — urgent

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed behaviour: KV cache evictions on shard-ranged allocation followed by backfilled cache storms on warm-up that produced high tail latency for sequences >512 tokens. Error spike is downstream tokenization timeouts in the runtime (partial responses).
- Likely trigger: an uneven traffic burst around 14:35 UTC combined with concurrent checkpoint compaction on the serving pool for that cluster.

Immediate mitigations applied:
1) Rolled a routing policy to route FR prod to a quantized model variant (q4_8) — reduces token cost and lowers latency on the tail. (Applied 15:40 UTC)
2) Short autoscale reserve (2x capacity) for the affected pool (expires 16:05 UTC).
3) Enabled prefix/KV cache warm-up prefetch for active customer keys.

Created SUP-9457 for the follow-up investigation (link in thread). Snapshot: initial_snapshot.json attached.

Will draft RCA for the account owner — recommended owners: Grace (runtime investigation), Markus (capacity/compaction policy), Kimberly (customer comms).

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

- Incident: 10/01/2027, ~14:35–14:57 UTC. Customer experienced 22-minute user impact window; peak error-rate delta +6% and median tail latency +450ms for long sequences.
- Root cause (preliminary): cache eviction + concurrent compaction + routing that didn't route traffic away from warm nodes.

A) Immediately offer a one-time credit equal to two days of usage (ask approval) — owner: Kimberly (customer-facing).
B) Infrastructure fixes: revise compaction schedule + implement proactive KV warm-up + modify routing to detect warm-up storms — owner: Markus / Grace. Timeline: mitigation sprint Oct 9–13.
C) Long-term: change default routing policy for high-traffic tenants and add a prefetch policy — product + infra to scope; ask for product priority slot.

Please reply with approval or comments. I recommend we approve the credit and commit the Oct 9 sprint.

-Markus

Sara / Michael —
Thank you again for your patience while we completed the internal investigation. Attached is the RCA and the corrective-action checklist (RCA_FastRetail_20271005.pdf and remediation-checklist.csv). High-level summary below and ask at the bottom.

Root cause (final):
- A cluster-level compaction job was scheduled in the same minute as an unanticipated traffic burst for your tenant. The compaction increased memory pressure on a subset of serving nodes, which triggered near-simultaneous KV cache evictions. When the workload returned, this produced a cache warm-up storm and elevated request latency; the runtime experienced tokenization timeouts leading to partial responses (error spike).

What we fixed (short-term):
- Compaction scheduling change to avoid vulnerable windows for high-traffic tenants.
- New routing guard that detects warm-node storms and routes traffic to warm spare nodes automatically.
- Short-term capacity reserved for your tenant during high-season windows (we've provisioned a weekly buffer through Q1 while we roll the long-term solution).

Planned longer-term actions (owners & ETA):
- Modify compaction orchestration and add pre-compaction drain for tenant-rich pools — owner: Markus; ETA: Oct 13
- Persistent KV warm-up and proactive caching heuristics — owner: Grace; ETA: Oct 15
- Routing policy change to default to adaptive warm-routing for tenants >X qps — owner: Product; ETA: Nov 1

Commercial ask and closure proposal:
- We propose a one-time credit equal to two days of average usage while we remediate. Please confirm approval by EOD Oct 6 so we can apply immediately.
- Request a 30-minute closure call the week of Oct 12 to validate fixes on a joint load test.

Please find attached: RCA_FastRetail_20271005.pdf (detailed timelines, event graphs, logs), remediation-checklist.csv (owners + delivery dates).

Thanks — we own this and will follow through on the timeline.
